name: Aerial 3-4-3

slots.why: Distributes long to the target men after winning the ball.
Wide centre-back who defends the channel behind the wing-back. Cover is the alternate.
Ball-playing defender in the centre starts moves with a pass out of defence. Central Defender (Defend) is the alternative: with more direct passing, the long ball does not need a specialist passer.
Wide centre-back on the right. Cover is the alternate, but only one Cover can be used.
Attacking wing-back gives the width and delivers the cross.
Defensive central midfielder protects the back three.
Supporting central midfielder links the defence with the forwards.
Attacking wing-back on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Wide target man (Attack) runs to the far post to attack the cross.
Wide target man (Attack) on the right, attacking the far post.
Target man (Support) attacks the near post and wins the flick-ons.

description: A 3-4-3 with attacking wing-backs supplying crosses for two wide target men and a central target man.
whyGood: The back three gives a solid base, and the two wing-backs and three tall forwards create a lot of crossing traffic in the box.
whyThisShape: Three centre-backs leave the two wing-backs free to push up the pitch and cross. The wide target men attack the far post and the target man attacks the near post, so each cross meets several players. The central midfield pair are the only midfielders, so the team relies on direct passing more than on possession.
whenToUse: When you have two wing-backs who cross well and three tall forwards, especially against a back four that struggles with aerial balls.
whenNotToUse: Against quick counter-attackers who target the space behind the wing-backs; and when you need to keep the ball, since the two midfielders will be outnumbered.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.More Direct Passing: Reach the physical or running outlets early and compete for the following ball.
instructionRationale.Hit Early Crosses: Deliver before the defensive line resets, using the target or forward runners already attacking the box.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Move the ball before the opponent resets, using the receivers and runners supplied by the roles.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Floated Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: Three centre-backs who defend the box
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
No forced Counter after a regain: the receiving and linking roles choose when to release the runners, rather than requiring every regain to become a break.
